title: A browser app a gallery can actually use
summary: Open Gallery now opens in the browser with works, artists, exhibitions, import review, publishing, look and settings, and backup. A second, week-later spreadsheet went through the review screen end to end in a headless browser: 3 new works, 20 updates, the stale sold work held as sold, and the near-duplicate blocked until someone chose what it was.
why: The engine only matters if a gallery owner can see and decide what changes. The import screen shows every column mapping and every row that needs a person, and nothing is saved until Apply.
detail: Each artwork page has a side panel showing exactly what the public would see and lists what is never shown. Private fields sit in a separately marked section. Exhibitions get their own order, text and layout plus a printable catalog that saves as PDF from the browser. Publishing makes web-sized copies of images in the browser before building, which also drops camera metadata from public files. The Artsy panel says plainly that there is no connection and offers an upload file and a manual checklist. Checked at desktop and phone widths with no horizontal scrolling and no console errors. Not yet checked: screen reader use and a real gallery's spreadsheet.
next: Finish the automated test suite (privacy scan, repeat imports, restore, failure cases, 1,500-work performance), then keyboard and accessibility checks.
author: Claude
